relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-readd
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - direction loosely applied: the source states rebalance must follow server-readd, not precede it; reconciliation may prefer a different predicate or direction
relations.evidence: Note that after the server-readd subcommand is run you must rebalance the cluster.

notable_absence.finding: Like server-add.md, server-readd.md gates the credentials of the node being ADDED BACK (--server-username/--server-password) but never states what role the operator RUNNING the command must hold on the existing cluster - despite this being a deprecated, cluster-topology-altering operation the page itself frames around recovering from failure/maintenance scenarios. Unlike node-reset.md (this same batch), which at least states 'requires full admin permissions' informally for a comparably consequential operation, server-readd states no role requirement of any kind.

cross_component_finding: server-readd.md's OPTIONS define the credentials of the node being added back as --server-username/--server-password ('This flag specifies the username for a user who has the ability to modify the cluster topology of the node being added back'). Its near-identical sibling couchbase-cli-server-add.md defines the semantically identical parameter - credentials for the node being added, described in almost the same words - as --server-add-username/--server-add-password instead. The two commands disagree on the flag name for the same concept, and (per server-add.json's own finding in this batch) server-add's own broken second EXAMPLE actually uses server-readd's naming by mistake. Separately, server-readd's SYNOPSIS omits --services and --index-storage-setting entirely (a re-added node keeps whatever services/storage mode it had before failover, unlike a freshly-added node via server-add) - a coherent design choice, but this page never explains WHY the flag set differs from server-add's, leaving the asymmetry unglossed.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none - server-readd is a self-managed Server failover-recovery operation with no Capella analog stated or implied on this page.
